(Bloomberg) -- A relentless tech-stock rally pushed the Nasdaq 100 Index toward its first record since June on Tuesday, extending gains fueled by bets on artificial intelligence tools from the likes of Meta Platforms Inc.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Stocks Jump on AI Optimism as AMD Tops $1 Trillion: Markets Wrap

AI Risk Is Everywhere and It's Making Billion Dollar Funds Nervous

The tech-heavy gauge advanced as much as 0.7% to 30,699, a level that exceededd its record close in June, before paring the gains. Shopify Inc. was the top-performing stock in the Nasdaq 100, climbing 7.0% after inking a partnership with Meta for its Muse AI product.

Trades rushed back into technology and growth stocks seen as the biggest beneficiaries from AI amid renewed hopes for diplomatic efforts to revive energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. The S&P 500 Index traded little changed and is hovering 0.5% away from its record in August, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.4%.

"What a rally," said Brad Conger, chief investment officer at Hirtle & Co. "For the past month or so I've felt like the market was incredibly strong even though it wasn't moving anywhere because it was coping with oil going up."

In the current market, investors are "more than willing to chase rallies when they occur," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers LLC. He added that investors have been unwilling to jump out of the tech sector. "During the modest selling occurred last week, it felt as though investors were only willing to lighten up, not truly liquidate their positions or take risk out of their portfolios."

Strategists see more bullishness in the AI trade even as a rally in chipmakers in Europe and Asia stalled overnight. Separately, Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. unveiled what it called China's most powerful AI chip, potentially enhancing competition with the US sector.

"The strong reception for Muse reignited enthusiasm across the AI hardware ecosystem," said Christopher Murphy, co-head of derivatives strategy at Susquehanna. He added that options flows signal "upside chasing" in the tech trade.

Energy stocks were broadly down as oil continued to slide after overnight headlines in Japan revealed that Iranian officials had proposed re-opening the Strait of Hormuz in seven days. Saudi Arabia also expects to resume operations on its 7-million-barrels-a-day East-West pipeline this week.

Recent gains in oil prices have also pushed up inflation expectations and yields, which have hampered equity performance. "We believe the stock market's gains for the year are in, and have reduced our S&P 500 target to 7,800 due to rising rates, which are a drag on stocks," said Emily Bowersock Hill, CEO of Bowersock Capital Partners.

All eyes are on US President Donald Trump's speech at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Trump called on the world to help the White House isolate Iran's economy in a campaign designed to pressure Tehran into ending the war.

In economic news, US private payrolls rose an average of 20,000 per week in the four week period to Sept. 5. General regional business activity slipped, according to a report from the Philadelphia Fed.

Sectors in Focus

Watch chipmakers after a rally in Europe and Asia stalled, with optimism over Meta Platforms Inc.'s personal agent giving way to caution in a sign that investors remain reluctant to chase gains after recent volatility.

Energy stocks are down 0.2%, given the decline in oil prices.

Watch shares Quest Diagnostics and Labcorp Holdings after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) released new preliminary medicare payment rates for lab services.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and SpaceX made the cut. Enter your email to see the other nine names and why SPCX earned its spot. The report is free. Enter your email and see the full list.

The third Friday of September marks a quiet ritual on Wall Street: the Nasdaq 100's quarterly rebalance. This month's version was not quiet. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), which joined the index in July after its IPO, saw its weighting more than double, according to CNBC's Morgan Brennan. Every fund tracking the Nasdaq 100, starting with the Invesco QQQ (NASDAQ:QQQ), is now a materially larger holder of a company its portfolio managers never chose.

Andrew Clemente

Nasdaq weights constituents by float-adjusted market capitalization. SpaceX's float expanded as post-IPO lockups expired, pushing the index weight higher. This same event that forces passive funds to buy also adds new supply to the market, making the demand story more fragile than headlines suggest.

If you own a Nasdaq 100 fund, you own more SPCX than you did last week. A formula decided that.

What Actually Changed in the Index

The Nasdaq 100 is reweighted quarterly in March, June, September, and December after the close of trading on the third Friday, using prior-month data. No issuer may exceed 24% of the weight.

Index weight scales with float-adjusted market cap. When SpaceX entered in July, only a portion of its shares were public. As lockups rolled off through August and September, the public float grew, and Nasdaq's September recalculation caught up.

The agency said the proposed changes were intended to realign Medicare payments with private-insurer rates and were based on the same analysis of more than 6,400 laboratories.

Investing.com - The Nasdaq 100 posted its best session since early August on Monday, surging 2.8% to a record close as investors concluded that AI-driven earnings growth has made the Federal Reserve's latest rate hike a secondary concern.

Still guessing which names to buy? Our AI rebuilds its stock picks at the start of every month. The list is beating the market by 120%. See what's on it »

AI infrastructure spending seems to be moving from narrative to revenue, and the companies building the picks and shovels are being repriced accordingly. Meta added approximately 12% on the same session, boosted by the breakout success of its AI agent app Muse.

On the other hand, U.S. crude oil tumbled 4.5% and Brent fell 3.4%, pulling the 10-year Treasury yield down more than four basis points to 4.95%.

Lower energy prices ease the inflation outlook directly; a falling long yield loosens the discount rate applied to growth stocks' future cash flows. Both moves arrived as a gift to the Nasdaq's most rate-sensitive names.

The Fed raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points last week to a target range of 3.75%-4.00%, its first rate increase since 2023. Projections released alongside that decision show the policy rate peaking at 4.00%-4.25% by year-end before holding steady through 2027 — a terminal rate well below the 5.5% ceiling hit in the prior tightening cycle.

That ceiling matters because long-duration equities are extraordinarily sensitive to where rates stop, not just where they are going. A plateau at 4.25% is a fundamentally different environment than one at 5.5%.

The Bank of Japan raised rates to a 31-year high of 1.25% last week, the European Central Bank has hiked twice in 2026, while the Reserve Bank of Australia has raised three times this year to 4.35%. The pace is calibrated rather than the emergency campaign that followed Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and markets are treating it as such.

Market focus shifts from rates and oil to Trump-Xi summit

The week's central event is the Trump-Xi summit scheduled for Thursday at the White House. Boeing orders, rare earths, and AI regulation are all on the agenda, with markets focused above all on whether the U.S.-China tariff truce, currently set to expire on November 10, will be extended into 2027.

A truce extension would remove the single largest binary risk overhanging U.S. multinationals and could serve as the trigger for a broader year-end equity advance before November midterm election results reshuffle the fiscal policy outlook.
